# @zakkster/lite-ring-buffer

> Pre-allocated, zero-GC circular buffer over a Float32Array. Power-of-two capacity, mask-based wrap, oldest-first bulk copy.

## Summary

`@zakkster/lite-ring-buffer` is a zero-dependency ESM micro-library that maintains a sliding window of float32 samples without allocating during steady-state operation. It is designed for telemetry windows (frame times, audio amplitudes, network RTT, mouse velocity) where the naive `Array.push + Array.shift` pattern produces O(n) shifts and per-frame GC pressure.

The buffer is backed by a single `Float32Array` whose length is the next power of two >= the requested capacity. Wrap-around uses a bitmask AND (`head & mask`) instead of a modulo. The hot-path `push(value)` performs one indexed store, a masked increment and a compare, with no allocation.

## Core API

```js
import { RingBuffer } from '@zakkster/lite-ring-buffer';

const rb = new RingBuffer(1024);            // capacity rounded up to next pow2
rb.push(42);                                // O(1), zero alloc
rb.peekNewest();                            // -> 42
rb.peekOldest();                            // -> 42 (only one sample)
rb.count;                                   // -> 1
rb.capacity;                                // -> 1024
rb.isFull();                                // -> false

const out = new Float32Array(rb.count);
rb.copyTo(out, 0);                          // oldest-first; out[0] = oldest
```

## Concepts

- **Capacity** is rounded up to the next power of two so wrap-around can use a bitmask. The original request is preserved on `.requestedCapacity`.
- **`get(offset)`** uses 0 for newest, `count-1` for oldest. Returns `undefined` if out of range. Its `number | undefined` result boxes a non-integer sample (16 B per call); in a hot loop use **`getOrDefault(offset, 0)`**, which allocates nothing.
- **`pushBatch(src, srcOffset = 0, count = src.length - srcOffset)`** pushes `count` samples from a `Float32Array` / `Float64Array` `src` and returns `count`. The result is the state of `count` calls of `push` (same `data` slots, `head`, `count`; values round through float32, read back as the same values by `Object.is`, NaN payload bits unspecified). `count` > `capacity` keeps the last `capacity` samples; `count` 0 is a no-op after validation. Allocates nothing for a Float32Array / Float64Array `src` while each family's load / store site has seen at most 4 `src` hidden classes (Node 26.8.2 arm64; DETERMINISTIC, `npm run alloc`). Errors (nothing written): `TypeError` for a `src` that is not a TypedArray or is any other TypedArray than Float32Array / Float64Array (BigInt kinds included, even at count 0), for count > 0 a `this.data` that is not a Float32Array (intrinsic tag, every call; the `capacity`-slots RangeError is checked first), and, for count > 0, a frozen ring (`Object.freeze`, from the `head` store); `RangeError` for `srcOffset` / `count` not non-negative integers (no coercion, no user `valueOf`) or `srcOffset + count > src.length` (checked before the element-type check), and for count > 0 a `data` that does not hold `capacity` slots or a `src` sharing the ring's ArrayBuffer. Only a whole-ring `Object.freeze` is covered: per-property tampering (a non-writable `count` alone, accessors on `head` / `count` / `data`) is unsupported and may leave `head` written, as with `push`. After `destroy()`, with valid arguments, it returns `count` and stores nothing (like `push`; invalid arguments still throw); a detached or out-of-bounds `src` reads as length 0 (`count` omitted -> 0, explicit `count` >= 1 -> `RangeError`). A sealed ring works. The alias cache is shared with `copyTo`.
- **`copyTo(dst, dstOffset)`** writes oldest-first. Allocates nothing at any size while each of its three store sites (Float32Array `dst`, Float64Array `dst`, every other element type) has seen at most 4 distinct `dst` hidden classes in the process; past that the site boxes every non-integer sample (16 B each, Node 26.8.2 arm64; `copyToFast` is unaffected). A full Float32 ring of more than 32 samples is one `set` + `copyWithin` rotation plus a loop over the smaller half; every other copy is a masked scalar loop. A `dst` that is not a TypedArray (an Array, a DataView, a plain object) throws `TypeError`; a too-small one, one sharing the ring's ArrayBuffer (an aliasing BigInt64Array / BigUint64Array included), or (count > 0) a ring whose `data` was replaced, resized or detached so it no longer holds `capacity` slots, throws `RangeError`. Nothing is written in any case. The alias check is ArrayBuffer identity: two SharedArrayBuffer objects over one memory block are not detected. A frozen or sealed ring copies correctly (the array cached before the lock stays referenced until `destroy()`, or for the ring's lifetime when frozen). A small (<= 64 B) on-heap `dst` has its ArrayBuffer materialized once by the alias check (about 32-61 B off-heap per fresh small `dst`, REPORTED): reuse `dst`.
- **`copyToFast(dst, dstOffset)`** has the same result, validation and errors, but copies with at most two `set` calls over `subarray` views, so it allocates 104 B (contiguous) or 208 B (wrapped) per call (not affected by the 4-class limit; detached storage is a `RangeError`). Use it when large wrapped or partly filled Float32 copies are hot and that allocation is acceptable.
- **`copyLast(dst, dstOffset, n)`** writes the newest `k = min(n, count)` samples oldest-first into a Float32Array / Float64Array from `dstOffset` (`undefined` means 0) and returns k; `n` is required (omitted is a `RangeError`). Checks in order, all before the first store: `TypeError` (`dst` not a TypedArray), `RangeError` (`n` not a non-negative integer, no coercion), `RangeError` (bounds on `dstOffset + n`, not k: an `n` larger than `dst` can hold throws even on an empty ring), return 0 when k is 0 (before the alias and storage checks), `RangeError` (alias), `RangeError` (storage), then the first store (a BigInt64Array / BigUint64Array `dst` with k > 0 throws `TypeError` there). Nothing is written on any throw. `copyLast(dst, off, rb.count)` writes, returns and throws exactly as `copyTo(dst, off)` (the messages name `copyLast`). For a whole-window copy `copyTo` is the safe choice: parity ratio medians are 0.99-1.02 over two strict runs, with a one-off slow compilation at head 768 in each (Float32 1.18 in strict-1, Float64 1.19 in strict-2; every other compilation median <= 1.05) (REPORTED, `npm run bench:copylast`, two `quiet-lock run --strict` runs 2026-11-15T05:55Z and 06:08Z (exit 0 both), Apple M4 Pro, Node v26.8.2 / V8 14.6.202.34-node.28, host QUIET, K 21 x 3 compilations = 63 paired rounds per row; parity is not guaranteed, it depends on the caller's inlining budget). Against copying the whole window and then its last n, `copyLast` is 2.1x faster (Float32) / 2.2x (Float64) at n 120 and 1.5x (Float32) / 1.2x (Float64) at n 512 of a full 1024 ring (REPORTED, the lower of the two strict runs). The thrown error for every input is unchanged from 1.5.0 (same order); a view `dst` sees exactly one `dst instanceof DataView` per call (a user `DataView[Symbol.hasInstance]` runs once). Only replaced builtins can tell the difference from 1.5.0: `n` / `dstOffset` are tested before the DataView check, a failing call may call the global `ArrayBuffer.isView` / `Number.isInteger` more often, and a bounds failure with a valid `dstOffset` reads `dst`'s length twice. The checks use the global `ArrayBuffer.isView`, `Number.isInteger`, `DataView` and `Object.isExtensible`, and the `call` of the intrinsic length and `buffer` getters, at call time (`copyLast`'s store dispatch, after the checks, also calls the `Symbol.toStringTag` getter's `call`; `copyLastFast` never does); replacing any of them, or anything that changes what those getters' `call` resolves to (replacing or deleting `Function.prototype.call`, an own `call` property on a getter, or a changed prototype of a getter), is unsupported (out of contract). The call-time lookups of every bulk method are listed in the "Call-time lookups" bullet below. `copyLast` is kept inlinable into its caller: the inlined chain copyLast + `lastCheck` + `rotCopy` is 765 B of bytecode, within V8's 766 B cumulative-inlining reserve on Node v26.8.2 / V8 14.6.202.34-node.28 (1.5.0: 791 B), gated by `test/chainsize.test.js` (DETERMINISTIC, pinned engine). Allocates 0 B while each of its three store sites (Float32Array `dst`, Float64Array `dst`, every other element type) has seen at most 4 distinct `dst` hidden classes in the process; the sites are its own, not `copyTo`'s, EXCEPT the whole-window Float32 path (a full ring copied whole, capacity > 32), which runs `copyTo`'s `rotCopy`: that store site is shared with `copyTo`, so every Float32 `dst` class either method passes through `rotCopy` counts against one 4-class budget.
- **`copyLastFast(dst, dstOffset, n)`** has the same result, validation order and errors as `copyLast`, but copies with at most two `set` calls over `subarray` views, so it allocates one view per ring half it spans (REPORTED 104.0 B contiguous / 208.0 B straddling, `npm run alloc`, 2026-11-15, Node v26.8.2 arm64) and never boxes a sample, whatever the number of `dst` classes.
- **Call-time lookups of the bulk methods (out of contract if replaced).** `copyTo`, `copyToFast`, `copyLast`, `copyLastFast` and `pushBatch` capture the `%TypedArray%.prototype` getters (`length`, `buffer`, `Symbol.toStringTag`) and the `set` / `copyWithin` methods once, at module load, so a prototype getter patched after load, or a subclass's own getter, cannot change what they read: that is a guarantee. They still resolve, at call time, each a subset per method: the globals `ArrayBuffer.isView`, `Number.isInteger`, `DataView` (the `instanceof` check) and `Object.isExtensible` (only when the call has at least one sample to copy or push, on an alias-cache miss); `Math.min`, `data.subarray` and the `data.constructor` / `Symbol.species` lookups `subarray` itself makes (the two Fast methods only); on a throw, the globals `TypeError` and `RangeError` (and `String` for a bounds message in the four copy methods); and the `call` of every captured intrinsic getter and method (`Function.prototype.call` unless the intrinsic has its own or inherited `call`). User code installed on any of these can run inside a call, outside the one `DataView` window `copyLast` documents (`instanceof` also walks `dst`'s prototype chain, so a Proxy there runs its trap). Replacing any of those globals or builtins, or anything that changes what an intrinsic's `call` resolves to (replacing or deleting `Function.prototype.call`, an own `call` property on an intrinsic, a changed prototype of an intrinsic), is unsupported (out of contract).
- **`tryPush(value, options)`** mirrors `push` but returns `false` when the buffer is full and `options.overwrite === false`. The options argument is read by property access -- no destructuring default -- so `tryPush(v)` does not allocate.
- **`reset()`** clears the buffer and fills the backing storage with zeros so consumers that read `data` directly never see old samples.
- **`forEach(fn)` / `[Symbol.iterator]`** visit samples oldest-first, matching `copyTo`. Zero allocation with a hoisted callback holds for ONE callback function per process: a second distinct callback makes the call site megamorphic (about 128 B per 8-sample call, REPORTED).
- **`ceilPow2(n)`** and **`MAX_CAPACITY`** (2^31) are exported helpers. Capacities above 2^31 throw `RangeError` (a null-prototype object or an object with a throwing `toString` as capacity or `dstOffset` throws `TypeError` / the user's error instead). `ceilPow2` is not validated: a finite `n` in (-2^31, 0] gives 2^32; at or below -2^31 the uint32 wrap decides (`ceilPow2(-(2 ** 31)) === 2 ** 31`).
- **`destroy()`** swaps the backing typed array for a shared empty `Float32Array` (not `null`) so the GC can reclaim it in long-lived applications. Calls after `destroy()` are undefined behavior; `push`, `tryPush` and `reset` no longer throw, they do nothing.

## Constraints

- ESM only.
- Stores `number` values that round-trip through float32. Integers up to 2^24 are exact; larger integers lose precision (a monotonic energy counter in Wh crosses 2^24 = 16,777,216, so Wh totals belong in the caller's Float64 columns, not in this ring). A finite `|x| >= 2^128 - 2^103` (about 3.4e38, just past the float32 max 3.4028234663852886e38) stores as +/-Infinity: `push(1e39)` stores `+Infinity` although `1e39` passes `v === v`, so input NaN / finite checks do not predict the stored value.
- `push` / `tryPush` coerce like a typed-array store: `null`, `''` and `[]` store 0, `undefined` stores NaN (map missing readings to NaN yourself).
- NaN and +/-Infinity are stored and read back unchanged. Downstream consumers must filter NaN where it matters (e.g. min/max).
- After `destroy()` the instance is unusable.
- Not thread-safe and not shareable across Workers: `head` and `count` are instance fields, not shared memory, and a consumer that takes samples off would have to write `count` too. Cross-thread streaming needs a different structure, an SPSC ring: two monotonic wrapping indices in a `SharedArrayBuffer` header, each written by one side (`Atomics.store`) and read by the other (`Atomics.load`); occupancy `(w - r) >>> 0`, slot `idx & mask`; the indices on separate cache lines, 128 B apart. This package is not that structure (a separate package if ever wanted).

## Performance

- `push`, `tryPush(v)`, `getOrDefault(i, 0)` and `peek*` are O(1) and allocate 0 B per call in a hot loop where V8 inlines them (`npm run alloc`, Node 26.8.2; the inlining precondition is checked by `npm run inline-diff`, REPORTED, run by hand, not in `verify`). `get(i)` allocates 16 B per call on non-integer samples. `forEach` is 0 B with ONE hoisted callback per process. `pushBatch` is 0 B for a Float32Array / Float64Array `src` while each family's load / store site has seen at most 4 `src` hidden classes (DETERMINISTIC, `npm run alloc`, MEGA lanes included).
- `copyTo` is O(n) and allocates 0 B at every size while each store site has seen at most 4 `dst` hidden classes (past that: 16 B per non-integer sample; the family split is gated by the `npm run alloc` MEGA lanes; the residual is REPORTED; every gated lane <= 0.2 B per call against the < 1 B gate, `npm run alloc` inside `npm run verify`, 2026-11-12, Node 26.8.2 arm64). `copyToFast` allocates 104 B (contiguous) or 208 B (wrapped), REPORTED. `copyLast` allocates 0 B under the same per-store-site 4-class rule (every gated `copyLast` lane <= 0.2 B per call, `npm run alloc` inside `npm run verify`, 2026-11-15; the whole-window Float32 path shares `copyTo`'s `rotCopy` store site, so its `dst` classes count against one budget with `copyTo`); `copyLastFast` allocates one `subarray` view per ring half it spans (104 B contiguous / 208 B straddling, REPORTED). Dev-only `npm run bench:copylast` is the STATISTICAL copyLast A/B (not in `verify`, not shipped). Timing vs 1.2.1 is STATISTICAL and REPORTED (`npm run bench:copyto`, dev-only; one strict QUIET run 2026-11-12, Apple M4 Pro, Node v26.8.2, load1 2.74 at start, K 21 x 3 compilations): n = 32 is 1.47-1.52x slower; n = 64 and 128 are faster in every layout; a Float64 `dst` is faster at every n >= 64; Float32 rings are 1.29x (wrapped) / 1.34x (count n-1) slower at 256 and 3.03x (full, wrapped) / 3.85x (count n-1) slower at 1024, where `copyToFast` is the faster choice.
- Wrap cost, REPORTED (`npm run bench:compare`, dev-only, not in `verify`, not shipped; one strict QUIET run 2026-11-15, Apple M4 Pro, Node v26.8.2, load1 2.62 at start / 1.68 at end, K 21 x 3 compilations): per wrap step, `% capacity` is 1.784x [1.759..1.829] the `& mask` step at the same power-of-two capacity (1024) and 5.630x [5.583..5.799] at a non-power-of-two one (1023); inside a hand-rolled Float32Array push, 1.057x [1.042..1.203] and 3.204x [3.186..3.249]. The README "Comparison (REPORTED)" table also has push / get / copyTo against hand-rolled rings and lite-o1 RingDeque.
- `npm run torture` (`test/torture.mjs`, dev-only): lite-leak retention (all 4096 churned instances tracked mid-run, exact count gated, then drained to tracker size 0; the backing `data` of 256 live instances is reclaimed after `destroy()`) and a lite-gc-profiler budget of major 0 / minor 0 over 2,000,000 ops on each of 6 gated lanes and 125,000 ops on each of two more (the `copyTo` 1024 lane and the `pushBatch 1024 set+slice+F64+over-cap` lane), with a control lane that must collect. `copyToFast`, `copyLastFast` and `get(i)` are reported, not gated. Two `copyLast` lanes are gated (`copyLast 120 straddling F32+F64`, 250,000 ops; `copyLast(count) ROT full 1024`, 125,000 ops). GC-count resolution is nominal: torture prints it as `res=` (the CONTROL lane's B/op divided by its minor-GC count) on the GATE line, and it depends on the V8 new-space size, so a gated lane reading minor 0 proves it allocates less than `res` B/op, not 0 B/op. `npm run alloc` is the per-op byte gate.
- 1M `push` calls into a 4096-slot buffer produce sub-MB heap growth (`npm test` = `node test/count.mjs`, count-gated: exactly 294 tests pass across `test/RingBuffer.test.js` (60), `test/InliningTool.test.js` (35), `test/copyto.test.js` (30), `test/copyto-r1b.test.js` (9), `test/audit-fix.test.js` (10), `test/mutant-kills.test.js` (10), `test/qa-r1.test.js` (15), `test/DeoptTool.test.js` (7), `test/pushbatch.test.js` (48), `test/qa-r2.test.js` (7), `test/copylast.test.js` (19), `test/copylast-parity.test.js` (9), `test/qa-r3.test.js` (22), `test/chainsize.test.js` (5; needs the pinned engine Node v26.8.2 / V8 14.6.202.34-node.28, fails on any other Node), `test/copylast-hooks.test.js` (4) and `test/qa-m1.test.js` (4), 0 fail, 0 skipped or todo, so an empty, skipped, crashed or early-exiting file fails; it runs under `--expose-gc`; the smoke test fails, not skips, when gc is not exposed; `npm test` needs exactly Node v26.8.2 / V8 14.6.202.34-node.28 (`test/chainsize.test.js` fails closed on any other Node), the other dev scripts need Node >= 24 (`test/alloc.mjs` reads V8's `total_allocated_bytes`), and the runtime `engines` field stays >= 18).

## Companion libraries

- `@zakkster/lite-stats-math` -- single-pass avg/min/max/quantile over a `RingBuffer`.
- `@zakkster/lite-canvas-graph` -- zero-GC `<canvas>` waveform renderer that consumes a `RingBuffer` directly.
